_notes: 20 frames at 200 ms, voice 0.5 everywhere. Both mouths stay at 0.1, so lip activity is 0: with lips alone nobody is a candidate and the plan would be wide voice-only.
speaking: A (x 400) is 0.9 on frames 0-9 and 0.1 from 10; B (x 1300) the opposite.

speakingAt is the mean over real sightings within 500 ms (frames i-2..i+2). A: 0.9 up to frame 7, 0.74 on 8, 0.58 on 9, 0.42 on 10, 0.26 on 11, 0.1 from 12. B mirrors it: 0.42 on 9, 0.58 on 10, 0.74 on 11, 0.9 from 12.
A candidate needs speaking >= 0.5. Score = (0.6 speaking + 0.05 continuity) / 0.65 (no pan).

Frame 0: A is the only candidate and becomes current. Frame 10: B 0.535, A 0.465; B doesn't beat A by 0.15. Frame 11: B 0.683 > A 0.317 + 0.15, so B claims from frame 11 (2.2 s) and keeps the claim. Balanced hold 1 s: at frame 16 B takes over, back-dated to frame 11.
No overlap: on frames 9-10 only one face reaches 0.5.
Segments: A [0, 2.2 s), B [2.2 s, 4 s), both over the 1 s minimum. The reason stays lips+voice.
Window and keys as in plan-two-speakers: x 500 for A, 1400 for B, y 540, h 1080, one cut key per segment.
